open_points.subject: Cabinet context access
open_points.text: “Each authenticates with its own service token (R0-27), validates a project id and reads its context in the disclosure class its token allows” conflicts with R0-43: “`context` ... answers only a trusted service whose token allows `personal_data` — today PresuPro and Client Portal.”
open_points.question: Does Cabinet read any project context, and if so through which declared operation and disclosure class?
options: Cabinet does not read context
Cabinet receives the existing full `personal_data` context
Cabinet receives a separate non-personal projection
open_points.default_guess: Cabinet validates project ids but does not read context.

open_points.subject: Mixed-disclosure project outputs
open_points.text: R0-26 says “Registry offers separate outputs or a dedicated projection rather than one mixed answer,” while R0-43 keeps `context` and project-card answers containing both ordinary identity fields and the object's `personal_data` address.
open_points.question: Are the full project card and `context` each one wholly `personal_data`-classified output, or must their personal and non-personal fields be split into separate outputs?
options: Classify each whole answer as `personal_data`
Split personal and non-personal fields into separate outputs
Allow mixed fields with per-field disclosure classes
open_points.default_guess: Classify the whole full-context or project-card answer as `personal_data`, while keeping the agent projection separate.

open_points.subject: WhatsApp preparation
open_points.text: “the agent emits the link without a number and the owner picks the contact, or the owner interface supplies the number to the owner”
open_points.question: Which of these two workflows is Registry required to support, and what observable owner-interface action exists if Registry supplies the number?
options: Registry does nothing; the agent emits a numberless link and the owner selects the contact elsewhere
The owner interface provides the customer's number or completed link
Both workflows are required
open_points.default_guess: Registry provides no WhatsApp-specific action; the agent emits a numberless link.

open_points.subject: Rooms of an anonymised project
open_points.text: R0-62 says an anonymised project keeps “its id, status and artifact pointers and nothing else” and specifies erased answers for project, context and projection reads, but `list rooms` specifies only the unknown-project failure.
open_points.question: What does `list rooms` return for an anonymised project whose rooms were removed?
options: An erased-project refusal
An empty room list
Not found
The former rooms remain readable
open_points.default_guess: Return the same erased-project refusal used by the other non-artifact reads.

open_points.subject: Audit coverage
open_points.text: R0-58 records “changes to projects and customer records” and R0-37 permits the acting principal to be “agent through Kernel,” but R0-58 also says “Ordinary reads, agent calls and the inner steps of flows are not recorded.”
open_points.question: Exactly which state-changing actions are audited, especially agent-authority room and artifact changes, session registration and active-project changes, pending-request changes, imports, and automatic grant removals caused by project erasure?
options: Audit every accepted state-changing primary action
Audit only the categories explicitly enumerated in R0-58
Exclude every agent-authority call even when it changes state
Treat imports and cascading changes as single aggregate audit events
open_points.default_guess: Audit every accepted significant state change, including agent-originated changes, while excluding reads and non-changing flow steps; record one aggregate entry for each atomic action.

open_points.subject: Revision and access-version concurrency
open_points.text: R0-29 says “Every change ... made against an older revision is refused,” R0-35 gives revisions only to projects and customers after R0-45, and `read the session's access` introduces “the access version” without saying what changes it or which mutations must present it.
open_points.question: Which state-changing actions require an expected revision or access version, which version does each use, and which actions advance each version?
options: Only project and customer mutations use optimistic concurrency; access version is informational
Session grant, revoke, active-project and request-answer mutations use the access version as their concurrency token
Every owner-interface mutation, including imports and audit erasure, has a concurrency token
open_points.default_guess: Project and customer mutations use their record revisions; session-access mutations use the access version; append-only or bulk confirmed actions use their own idempotency or confirmation mechanism.
